newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's EDP slides, may bottom out.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's EDP slides, may bottom out.

text.p: Shares in state-controlled utility EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, the biggest stock on the market, were down 1.56 percent at 3,102 but traders said the fall of recent sessions could be nearing its end.

They saw some support at 3,100 and stronger support at 3,000 escudos per share. The utility has lost around 180 escudos over the past week on persistent selling triggered by a number of factors, traders said.
"The 3,000 escudos is a very strong support. It would be very strange for it to break as many people have that as a reference price to buy," said one trader.
"But the first level of support is 3,100," he added.

One factor depressing the price has been the prospect of some 60 million shares from the June privatisation coming on to the market from small investors and employees who had to hold them for three months.
These shares were bought at a discount of some six percent to the privatisation price of 2,250 escudos.
Traders said the selling in recent days had come from domestic players as well as non-residents.
